how_to_apply: Visit the official University of Delhi website at www.du.ac.in.
Open the Work with DU section.
Locate Advertisement No. R&P/323/2026 for Senior Assistant and Assistant posts.
Read the complete advertisement, eligibility criteria and general instructions.
Open the advertisement-specific online application form provided by the University.
Enter the required personal, educational qualification and work experience details.
Provide the relevant reservation and age-relaxation information, if applicable.
Upload the prescribed certificates and supporting documents according to the application portal instructions.
Pay the applicable application fee unless eligible for exemption under the previous advertisement provision.
Verify all information and complete the online submission within the applicable deadline.
Save the submitted application and fee receipt for future reference.

Important: Candidates must ensure that their educational qualifications, experience and age requirements are satisfied as of the applicable closing date. The University may initially accept applications provisionally and verify eligibility during subsequent recruitment stages.
important_instructions: The following rules apply to the preliminary examination and final selection process.

The Preliminary Examination is conducted in English and Hindi. Candidates may answer in either language but must use the same language throughout. Each preliminary question carries two marks, with a deduction of 0.5 mark for every incorrect answer. The preliminary qualifying cut-off is calculated using 50% of the average score of the top 5% of candidates, subject to the alternative calculation specified where fewer than two candidates qualify for that group. The notification allows 5% relaxation in the qualifying cut-off for SC/ST and 10% for PwBD candidates. Shortlisting for the Main Examination follows the prescribed vacancy-based ratio, with tied candidates at the cut-off also shortlisted. Final merit is based on the Main Examination, subject to qualifying the Skill Test and eligibility verification. Eligible candidates in the specified PwBD categories receive 20 minutes of compensatory time per hour.
The examination scheme provides an additional marks provision for eligible contract, ad hoc and temporary employees of the University of Delhi and its colleges.
Eligible employees may receive one additional mark per year of service, up to 10 marks, in the preliminary examination and final merit calculation, subject to the notified conditions.
The provision applies to employees covered by the notification who were working in the University or its colleges as of 25 March 2021.

content_sections.heading: Delhi University Vacancy Details 2026
content_sections.text: The University of Delhi has advertised 126 vacancies for Senior Assistant and Assistant posts. The PwBD reservations are horizontal and included within the notified vacancies. Applicants from UR, SC, ST, OBC and EWS categories may claim eligible PwBD reservations, subject to the disability conditions. The notification states that if an identified PwBD vacancy remains unfilled, one corresponding UR vacancy will be kept vacant.

content_sections.heading: Delhi University Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Candidates must possess the prescribed educational qualifications and work experience on the applicable closing date. Eligibility differs between Senior Assistant and Assistant posts. Experience Requirement: Candidates must have three years of experience as Assistant or equivalent in Level 4 in Central/State Government, universities, PSUs or Central/State Autonomous Bodies. Equivalent-pay experience in reputed private companies or corporate banks having a minimum annual turnover of Rs. 200 crore is also permitted under the notification. Experience Requirement: Candidates must have two years of experience as Junior Assistant or equivalent in a university, research establishment, Central/State Government, PSU or autonomous body. Equivalent-pay experience in reputed private companies or corporate banks with a minimum annual turnover of Rs. 200 crore is also permitted. Typing Requirement: Assistant applicants must have the prescribed English or Hindi typing speed. Typing proficiency forms part of the qualifying skill assessment.

content_sections.heading: Delhi University Recruitment 2026 Age Limit
content_sections.text: Age relaxation is applicable to eligible SC, ST, OBC (Central List), PwBD, ex-servicemen and other specified categories according to Central Government orders adopted by the University of Delhi. Eligible applicants with at least three years of regular service in the same or allied field in prescribed government, university, autonomous or PSU organizations may receive relaxation up to five years or the number of completed years of qualifying service, whichever is less. The prescribed direct-recruitment upper age limit is not insisted upon for eligible departmental candidates of the University or its colleges. Specified University/college contractual, daily-wage or ad hoc employees with at least one year of service may receive a one-time exemption, subject to the conditions in the notification. The special exemption does not extend to employees working through outsourced agencies or project-based contract assignments. Candidates claiming relaxation must submit the prescribed supporting documents during the relevant verification stages.

content_sections.heading: Delhi University Recruitment 2026 Selection Process
content_sections.text: Both posts follow a two-stage recruitment framework consisting of preliminary shortlisting and final assessment. Stage 1: Preliminary MCQ Examination for shortlisting candidates. Stage 2: Descriptive Main Examination followed by a qualifying Skill Test. Verification of educational qualifications, experience, reservation claims and other supporting documents. Final merit preparation according to Main Examination performance, subject to qualifying the Skill Test and prescribed rules. Merit Clarification: The Preliminary Examination is used only for shortlisting and does not carry weightage in the final assessment. The Skill Test is qualifying in nature.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are available in Delhi University Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The University of Delhi has advertised 126 vacancies, including 46 Senior Assistant and 80 Assistant posts.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to submit the application form?
faq.answer: The last date for receipt of the application is 09.11.2026 or within two weeks from the date of publication of the advertisement in the Employment News, whichever is later.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is required for Senior Assistant?
faq.answer: Candidates must possess a Bachelor's Degree and three years of the prescribed experience as Assistant or equivalent. Computer application, noting and drafting proficiency are also required.

faq.question: Q4. What qualification is required for Assistant?
faq.answer: Applicants need a Bachelor's Degree, two years of prescribed experience and English typing at 35 WPM or Hindi typing at 30 WPM, along with computer proficiency.

faq.question: Q5. Can fresh graduates apply for Delhi University Assistant posts?
faq.answer: No. Both advertised posts require the prescribed work experience in addition to graduation.

faq.question: Q6. What is the maximum age for Senior Assistant?
faq.answer: The maximum age is 35 years, subject to applicable relaxations.

faq.question: Q7. What is the maximum age for Assistant?
faq.answer: The maximum age is 32 years, subject to applicable relaxations.

faq.question: Q8. What is the application fee?
faq.answer: The fee is Rs. 1,000 for General/UR, Rs. 800 for OBC (NCL), EWS and female applicants, and Rs. 600 for SC, ST and PwBD applicants. Eligible candidates who applied under Advertisement R&P/311/2024 are exempt.

faq.question: Q9. What is the selection process?
faq.answer: Selection includes a Preliminary MCQ Examination for shortlisting, a descriptive Main Examination and a qualifying Skill Test. Final merit is prepared according to the notified examination rules.

faq.question: Q10. Is there negative marking?
faq.answer: Yes. The preliminary examination deducts 0.5 mark for each incorrect answer.
